paper_sections.title: Comparison of Hemodynamic Brain Responses Between Big Wave Surfers and Non-big Wave Surfers During Affective Image Presentation
Patterns of Signal Change During Negative-Valence IAPS Image Presentation
Differences in PPI Between BWS and CON During HANS Presentation

description.value: The study compared hemodynamic brain responses and task-related functional connectivity between big wave surfers and non-big wave surfers while they viewed affective images.

design.value: A cross-sectional between-group fMRI study using an event-related affective image presentation task and generalized psychophysiological interaction analysis.

description.value: Measured participants’ subjective emotional responses to the IAPS images.
Measured self-reported levels of sensation seeking across intensity and novelty of experience scales.
Assessed positive and negative feelings experienced over the past week.
Assessed self-reported levels of fear toward various circumstances, objects, or other stimuli.
Those who regularly surfed waves >20 feet in height using the Hawaiian measurement system.
Those who had not surfed waves of >20 feet in height using the Hawaiian measurement system.

task_description.value: Participants viewed 160 IAPS images categorized by valence and arousal, plus 20 fixation trials, for 180 randomized trials lasting 7.5 minutes.

design_type.value: event-related design with jittered inter-stimulus interval

instructions.value: Participants were asked to view all images presented on the screen. No tasks related to regulation were instructed.

stimuli.value: International Affective Picture System photographs; 40 images in each of high arousal positive, high arousal negative, low arousal positive, and low arousal negative groups.

task_performance_measures.value: After the fMRI, participants were asked whether they were able to remain attentive to all images.

instrument.value: 3 T MRI scanner (Achieva, Philips, Best, Netherlands)

description.value: Multi-shot gradient echo echoplanar imaging sequence; 22 axial slices covering the whole brain; bandwidth=56.6 Hz/pixel; flip angle=75°; field of view=240×240 mm; matrix=64×62; slice thickness=5 mm with no gap.

pulse_sequence_type.value: multi-shot gradient echo echoplanar imaging (EPI) sequence

instrument.value: 3 T MRI scanner (Achieva, Philips, Best, Netherlands)

description.value: Gradient echo sequences in the sagittal plane with TR=8.1 ms, TE=3.7 ms, bandwidth=191.4 Hz/pixel, flip angle=8°, field of view=240×240 mm, matrix=240×240, 145 slices, slice thickness=1 mm and no gap.

Images were realigned and slice-time corrected; a mean functional image was constructed; mean images were co-registered with the structural image; structural images were segmented and normalized using affine registration followed by nonlinear transformation; normalization parameters were applied to functional images; images were smoothed with an 8 mm Gaussian kernel at full width at half maximum.

steps.value: construction of a mean functional image volume
co-registration with the high-resolution structural image
affine registration followed by nonlinear transformation
application of normalization parameters to functional images

hrf_model.value: canonical hemodynamic response function and its temporal derivative

model_settings.value: Image onset in each trial was modeled; six realignment parameters were entered; data were high-pass filtered with a 1/128 Hz cutoff; serial autocorrelation was corrected by a first-degree autoregressive AR(1) model.

Psychological regressors were HAP, HAN, LAP, LAN, and FIX; the physiological variable was the de-convolved neural signal from seed regions; interaction terms were generated separately for each condition; age was used as a covariate in group comparisons.

description.value: Trials in which no image was presented and participants viewed a fixation cross.

name.value: Main effect of group: BWS > CON

definition.value: Main effect of group: BWS > CON

interpretations.value: The BWS group showed significant increases in BOLD signal in the visual cortex, periaqueductal gray, hippocampus, frontal areas of cortex, and insula compared to the CON group.

name.value: Main effect of group: CON > BWS

definition.value: Main effect of group: CON > BWS

interpretations.value: The CON group showed significant increases in BOLD signal in the cerebellum, hypothalamus, and frontal motor regions compared with the BWS group.

name.value: Main effect of valence: negative > positive

definition.value: Main effect of valence: negative > positive

interpretations.value: Presentation of negative-valence images resulted in significant increases in signal intensity across all participants in the middle frontal gyrus, angular gyrus, and superior frontal gyrus.
Significantly increased activation was observed in the visual cortex and the insula of the BWS group compared with CON during the presentation of HAN images.

roi_definition.value: a hypothalamus from the WFU Pick Atlas 1

search_volume.value: hypothalamus from the WFU Pick Atlas 1

interpretations.value: During the presentation of HAN images, the CON group showed significantly increased activity in the hypothalamus when compared with responses from the BWS group.

roi_definition.value: a periaqueductal gray mask from the Harvard Ascending Arousal Network (AAN) Atlas

search_volume.value: periaqueductal gray mask from the Harvard Ascending Arousal Network (AAN) Atlas

interpretations.value: Significantly increased activation of the periaqueductal gray was observed in the BWS group compared with the CON group during LAN image presentation.
BWS > CON during HAN versus LAN showed significantly increased activation in the visual cortex.

name.value: Insula PPI of HAN vs. FIX: CON > BWS

definition.value: Insula PPI of HAN vs. FIX: CON > BWS

target_regions.value: orbitofrontal gyrus/insula, inferior frontal gyrus, temporal gyrus, precentral gyrus

model_representation_notes.value: The generalized PPI model included psychological regressors, the physiological variable of the region of interest, and PPI variables for HAP, HAN, LAP, LAN, and FIX.

interpretations.value: In the CON group, evidence of functional connectivity during HAN presentation was seen between the insula and the orbitofrontal, inferior frontal and superior temporal cortices, and the prefrontal gyrus.

name.value: Hypothalamus PPI of HAN vs. FIX: CON > BWS

definition.value: Hypothalamus PPI of HAN vs. FIX: CON > BWS

target_regions.value: orbitofrontal gyrus/insula, precentral gyrus, middle frontal gyrus, temporal gyrus

model_representation_notes.value: The generalized PPI model included psychological regressors, the physiological variable of the region of interest, and PPI variables for HAP, HAN, LAP, LAN, and FIX.

interpretations.value: During HAN image presentation, the CON group showed significantly increased PPI between the hypothalamus and the insula, superior temporal cortex, precentral gyrus, and middle frontal cortex.
